title: One slow product blocks the shop
scenario: Customers report slow or failed availability checks. Test whether slow Lighting inventory affects other products.
why: All products share one Storefront worker. Slow lamp checks make other requests wait. Requests that wait longer than 1000 ms fail before reaching Inventory.
reproduce: Record a healthy baseline and your hypothesis. Then add a 1500 ms Lighting inventory delay with no variation.
assignment: Assignment: Can you keep chair and desk available while lamp stock is delayed or unavailable?

fields.label: Healthy baseline and metric
fields.prompt: Record healthy stock, delivery information and relevant Grafana readings.

fields.label: Hypothesis and fault injection
fields.prompt: Which availability checks should keep working during the 1500 ms Lighting delay? What would disprove your hypothesis?

fields.label: Observe the fault’s blast radius
fields.prompt: Record Lighting inventory latency and customer impact. Include all the data from Grafana that changed compared to the baseline.

fields.label: Mitigation and reason
fields.prompt: Keep the delay active. Test a 400 ms Inventory timeout. Also test the timeout in combination with fallback and breaker. Explain each effect.

fields.label: Same-fault validation
fields.prompt: Keep the fault and traffic unchanged. Test whether your protection keeps customer results within the limits in your hypothesis. Compare with your baseline and record the evidence.

fields.label: Conclusion and cleanup
fields.prompt: Did you found a weakness? What improved, and what remains limited? Clear faults, restore defaults and verify recovery.

solution: Healthy: All products return live data quickly through one shared worker.
With +1500 ms Lighting latency and the default 3000 ms timeout, lamp checks succeed slowly. Chair and desk can exceed their 1000 ms queue deadline while the worker waits for the lamp.
With only a 400 ms timeout, the lamp check errors sooner and frees the worker. Chair and desk can load again. Timeout alone cannot supply missing lamp stock.

The breaker pauses failed lamp stock requests for five seconds, avoiding repeated 400 ms waits. Inventory fallback is optional for this challenge: it changes the lamp error to Stock unconfirmed, but does not free the worker sooner or improve chair and desk results.
Clear the fault, allow calls to finish, and verify live results for all three products.
